title: Four published blues of 1912
summary: The Dallas, Memphis, Baby Seals and other 1912 blues, and Lasses White's earlier piece.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: Well, that was a copyrighted publishing date on that was September 26, 1940.

You know, and they claim they're only, and during 1912, that's the evidence of the first published blues that we have. Yeah. I mean, as blues. Yeah. There were four of them that came out that year. There was a Dallas blues, Memphis blues. Baby Seals. Baby Seals blues.
Nigger blues. There are only four.
I called it Negro blues. That didn't get published, but that was ahead of Handys and it had 14 verses to the thing. And I think I heard the guy sing it when he was even born.
Lasses White? Lasses White. Leroy Lasses White. Singing a minstrel man.
Yeah, singing nigger blues. And he put it in the copyright office. So it proves. In the manuscript, you see. Beforehand, he published his. And the Dallas blues also got there a little.
The Dallas blues was written by Juan. Wasn't it Hart Juan? Hart Juan.
No, it was written by a woman. And Hart Juan published it first. And when it came out later, why it was by Hart Juan, he forgot to put her name on it.
So there was a point. I think it's very significant that the year 1912, you had four published blues in four separate cities really, weren't they?

They weren't published, but they were in existence by copyright. By copyright from four different sources. Now Baby Seals Blues was published in that same year, before Handys. But it was a song that put the blues into the song, you see. So it wasn't a 12 bar blues. But you can take the first 12 bars of the verse and stop right there and you've got 12 bar blues. But it goes right on from there, right along into the song, Baby Seals Blues. Well, that was published in Columbia, Missouri, I believe. And it was arranged by Artie Matthews. Artie Matthews arranged it. Same guy with the Worry Blues.

Yeah. But that wasn't really a blues. When was Worry Blues written? It was 14 or 15. Oh, it was, 15. About 15. No, it was. Well, it is a blues. Oh, it's a blues. Is it a blues? I thought it was more of a ragtime.
